content:
Goal
* First paragraph: Please change the second sentence to:

Part 1 can be found here: {{https://www.codingame.com/training/medium/lost-astronaut}}.

* Second paragraph: Please add a full stop (.) after "signals".

* Please add the following after the definition of [[CHECKSUM]]:

The two numbers are sent in decimal and are never subject to the conversion described above.

* Since [[STREAM]] may contain spaces, the statement that the transmitter "has also stopped sending the separators between values" could cause confusion. Please replace "The message contains only letters and spaces, so any value that decodes to something else is not a valid reading" with:

Spaces may appear in the stream because a space character can be transmitted literally. Such spaces must not be interpreted as separators between encoded values.

* Please rewrite the second-to-last paragraph as follows to consolidate the validity conditions:

A valid message must satisfy all the following conditions:
• It consists of exactly [[N]] characters.
• The sum of the ASCII codes of those characters equals [[CHECKSUM]].
• It contains only <<letters and spaces>>.

Input
* Please remove ", so read the whole line".

Constraints
* I'm *not* suggesting adding an explicit constraint on [[CHECKSUM]], as its bounds can be derived from the range of [[N]], the ASCII codes of the permitted message characters, and the endpoint-space restriction.

Cover picture
* Please upload a cover picture for this puzzle and for Part 1.

Cases
* Validator 6: Please modify the case such that the output contains at least one lowercase letter "z".

* Are all these scenarios covered by the current cases? If so, please give one example test and one example validator for each digit length.

  • 6-digit and 7-digit binary values.

  • 2-digit and 3-digit octal values.

* Are there any cases where the input stream contains any of the letters from "a" to "f" as literal characters instead of as part of an encoded hexadecimal value? If so, please list them.

* The streams in Pair 7 can be split at non-digit characters, whereas those in Pair 6 consist entirely of digits. From a complexity perspective, I'd expect Pair 6 to be placed last. What are your thoughts?

* Across all test cases, what's the range of the number of possible readings that need to be considered? An exact range or an approximate estimate would be helpful.

* To assess case coverage, could you please identify which scenarios are covered by each test case?

1. An alternative reading has both a different [[N]] and a different [[CHECKSUM]].

2. An alternative reading has the same [[N]] but a different [[CHECKSUM]].

3. An alternative reading has the same [[CHECKSUM]] but a different [[N]].

4. None of the above.

An alternative reading must decode the entire stream into letters and spaces only, regardless of whether it satisfies the specified [[N]] or [[CHECKSUM]]. A test case may cover more than one of the first three scenarios.

Thanks.
